neighbours.label: Totality quantification: the head right after a universal 'all' (or 'any and all'), vs partial quantifiers (some, several, many)
fire: The new owner promised to honour any and all debts left by the old firm.
In the sermon he said that all power belongs to the people.
The judge ordered that all records be sealed until the trial ended.
Our contract waives any and all claims arising from the event.
Seen from the summit, all roads seemed to lead toward the sea.
The new law removes all limits on how much a donor may give.
She insisted that all things be returned to their places by evening.
The update fixes all bugs reported since the spring release.
quiet: The new owner promised to honour some debts left by the old firm.
In the sermon he said that a little power belongs to the people.
The judge ordered that several records be sealed until the trial ended.
Our contract waives a few claims arising from the event.
Seen from the summit, two roads seemed to lead toward the sea.
The new law removes certain limits on how much a donor may give.
She insisted that most things be returned to their places by evening.
The update fixes three bugs reported since the spring release.

predictions: The word after 'all' / 'any and all' reaches 0.3-0.6; the same frame with 'some', 'several' or 'a few' stays under 0.15.
notes: Probe: 'any and all restrictions' 0.606, 'all things are pure' 0.598, 'all authority' 0.333, 'all exceptions' 0.327, 'all cultures' 0.193; 'some authority' 0.031, 'several restrictions' 0.076, 'many things are' 0.150.
